## Concrete finding

### B1 — Operational Git update failure still exits successfully (criterion 5)

**Location:** `plugins/deepmodebot/skills/deepmodebot/assets/github-app/local_updates.py:25-32,227-242,439-456`; `assets/github-app/bot.py:2591-2601`.

`git()` raises `RuntimeError` for any nonzero Git subprocess. `synchronize()` classifies that exception as `preserved` rather than `failed` for checkout targets. A checkout has no copy recovery journal, so this failure also leaves `incomplete` empty. The corrected CLI only exits nonzero for `error`, `incomplete`, or `action == "failed"`; consequently an attempted checkout update can fail while `bot.py update` exits **0**.

**Real reproduction:** `python -B .scratch/final-review/runtime.py updater` cloned an owned disposable checkout with local `core.longpaths=true` and `core.autocrlf=false`, selected canonical historical commit `d604b39ffe65eab5d7c4a3a57824a1745150ee09` on `main`, set canonical origin, and observed a clean status. An explicitly owned `.git/index.lock` represented an unavailable Git transaction boundary. The unmodified public CLI authenticated/read real canonical GitHub upstream and attempted synchronization. Its output reported `Unable to create .../.git/index.lock: File exists`, classified the target `preserved`, and exited **0**. The checkout stayed at the old SHA. Removing only the owned lock and invoking recovery produced `fast-forwarded`, exit **0**, to observed canonical main `6b00c9303eca4a856144af63dff3dc28149dbe69`.

This is not a fork/dirty/feature-branch refusal or a missing installed prerequisite: a clean eligible checkout reached a failing Git write. It violates the explicit corrective acceptance requirement that failed updates return nonzero and remain distinguishable from ordinary preserved candidates. No data-loss claim is made; the demonstrated defect is false-success CLI status and misleading target classification. The watcher correction is separate and rejects this `preserved` result for handover.

**Evidence:** `updater-observations.json`, `updater-commands.json`, `updater-index-lock.stdout.txt`, `updater-index-lock.stderr.txt`, `updater-failed-receipt.json`, `updater-head-after-lock.stdout.txt`, `updater-recovery.stdout.txt`, `updater-recovery-receipt.json`, and retained `runtime.py`, all beside this report.

**Required correction:** distinguish operational Git subprocess failures from deliberate safety refusals, classify the former failed, and exercise the actual checkout failure path through the public CLI. Preserve intentional fork/dirty/feature/unknown candidates without turning them into operational failures. Do not merely special-case the fixture's lock text.
